hook: A coach's stopwatch, a phone's motion sensor and a slow-motion video describe the same sprint in different ways: a table of times, a graph that climbs and flattens, a strip of frames. The exam asks you to move between all of them, and two graph rules do most of the work: slope down, area up.

prereq.q: What does the slope of a graph of y against x tell you?
options: How fast y changes per unit of x
The value of y at x = 0
The total of y times x
prereq.why: Slope = Δy/Δx, a rate, with units (y unit)/(x unit).

prereq.q: A cart's velocity changes from 2.0 m/s to 5.0 m/s in 1.5 s. What is its average acceleration?
If Δx ∝ t², how does Δx change when t doubles?

figure.caption: One motion in four representations. Read downward with slopes (x-t → v-t → a-t) and upward with areas (a-t → v-t → x-t).

chain.effect: the slope of the x-t graph at any instant is the velocity
the slope of the v-t graph is the acceleration, and the area under it is the displacement
the v-t graph is a straight line and the three kinematic equations apply

chain.cause: An object falls with air resistance negligible
chain.effect: its acceleration is g = 9.8 m/s² downward at every instant, even when v = 0 at the top

ideas: A motion diagram shows positions at equal times: growing gaps mean speeding up, shrinking gaps mean slowing down.
Slope of x-t = velocity. Slope of v-t = acceleration. Area under v-t = displacement. Area under a-t = change in velocity.
For constant acceleration: v = v₀ + at; x = x₀ + v₀t + ½at²; v² = v₀² + 2a(x − x₀). Pick the one that leaves out the quantity you neither know nor want.
Free fall: a = g = 9.8 m/s² downward (10 m/s² is accepted), on the way up, at the top and on the way down.
If the acceleration changes (nonuniform), the v-t graph curves. Describe it from the graph only; the equations do not apply.

misconception.wrong: At the top of its flight a ball thrown straight up has zero acceleration, because it stops for an instant.
misconception.right: Its velocity is zero for an instant, but the velocity is still changing, from upward to downward, at 9.8 m/s² each second. The acceleration is g downward at the top, as everywhere else in the flight.

summary: Motion can be shown as a motion diagram, x-t, v-t and a-t graphs, equations and words. Slopes go down the chain (x-t to v-t to a-t) and areas go up it. For constant acceleration, three kinematic equations apply, each missing one quantity; free fall is constant acceleration g downward.
